receipt.external_abi: scalar-only C functions; resource and multiple-result functions are internal
runtime_assumptions: Linux LP64 target with 64-bit pointers and size_t
C calloc returns null or an initialized nonaliasing allocation of the requested size
C malloc returns null or a fresh nonaliasing allocation of the requested size; bytes are initialized before read or remain unobserved
C free accepts a live allocation from calloc or malloc, or null
abort terminates execution; no cleanup after traps is promised
native compiler, linker, loader, libc and host hardware are trusted

protocol.allocation_scope: same source-level allocation/lifetime algorithms; each compiler may optimize according to its semantics
protocol.failure_policy: retain every scheduled attempt; failed or missing samples fail quality; no trimming or reruns
protocol.inference_scope: seven paired groups; log-ratio t bound assumes independent approximately normal group log ratios
limitations: two synthetic buffer workloads, not real-world application coverage
C/C++ internals are not established memory-safe
finite correctness checks are not semantic equivalence proofs
PGO holdout is disclosed and only excludes profile training; it is not an unseen benchmark population
protocol.ordering: rotate kernels by group; rotate backends by group plus original kernel index; reverse odd groups
protocol.pgo: Clang instrumentation; both kernels on training inventory only, then llvm-profdata merge and profile-use
protocol.rss_scope: Linux /proc/self/status VmHWM of post-exec driver; ru_maxrss retained separately because launcher high-water marks can survive exec
protocol.scope: Linux x86-64; two byte-owner kernels; finite successful-allocation inputs
protocol.search: none; fixed compiler configurations, zero optimizer search calls
protocol.tail_scope: empirical nearest-rank batch quantiles; not service p99 or population-tail confidence bounds
